set.approach: From the Applebee campground, take the trail that leaves the east side of camp and climbs north onto the moraine. Pass the first lake on its west side and the second on its east side, then continue straight north up the Crescent Glacier to the south face of the spire. Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier. The route starts off the same large ledge as Paddle Flake, a short scramble above the glacier, but a bit farther right, from a big boulder below a set of flakes.
set.descent_text: The routes of the McTech area share one descent: from the ridge crest, rappel the Westside Story line on the south face, which has chain anchors at its belays. The anchors are in the left-hand of the two big corners; the first rappel starts at the top of the route.

review.notes: Approach from the Crescent Spire area page (consistent with Bugaboo Spire page); location from route page; descent from Westside Story, Woza Moya and Subsevere pages.

set.descent_text: This is the rappel route for McTech Arete and its neighbours, so parties descend it from the summit ridge, using the chain anchors at its belays, and can leave it at any pitch if weather turns. Take care that the rope does not jam when pulling, particularly on the lower rappels.

set.descent_text: From the top, follow the ridge toward the northeast ridge of Bugaboo Spire and find the rappel stations marked by a small cairn; they lead down the Westside Story line on the south face.

set.descent_text: From the top of the ridge, walk east along it to the top of McTech Arete, then look down the south face for a chain anchor that is hidden from above. This begins the rappels of the McTech area, which follow the Westside Story line.

review.notes: Location and descent from its own page; rappel line confirmed on the Westside Story page.

set.approach: From the Applebee campground, take the trail that leaves the east side of camp and climbs north onto the moraine. Pass the first lake on its west side and the second on its east side, then continue straight north up the Crescent Glacier to the south face of the spire. Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier. The route starts high on the headwall: climb the first three pitches of Paddle Flake Direct to its bolted chain anchor, then cut left onto the left-angling seam that starts the route. The Direct line is the better access, with less rockfall from above.

review.notes: Approach only.

set.approach: From the Kain hut, hike down the trail toward the parking lot to the point where it crosses the main creek. Just before the trail descends into switchbacks, strike off across the meadows toward the ridge. Plenty of easy lines gain the crest, and after which you follow the crest to the summit.
set.descent_text: Descend the Northwest Ridge, which makes a pleasant traverse of the spire.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; Classic Grit page also names the NW ridge descent.

set.approach: From Applebee, head up toward the Crescent-Eastpost saddle, then follow a slanting ramp that crosses the steep west face of the spire to its end. The route starts there and climbs the pillar shown on the topo.
set.descent_text: The route reaches the Southwest Ridge, which leads to the summit. Descend the Northwest Ridge.

review.notes: Own page; NW ridge descent also on the Direct Southeast Ridge page.

set.approach: The route is on the face directly above the Applebee campground. Walk up to the foot of the face, stopping where the roofs meet the ground, and look up for the line of bolts.
set.descent_text: The route is bolted for rappelling, so parties descend it. Bolt stations make it easy to lower or rappel off if a storm arrives.

review.notes: Single page.

set.approach: The route is a short walk from the Applebee campground, on the shady morning side of the spire.
set.descent_text: Descent is easy, either by rappelling the route's anchors or by walking off.

review.notes: Single page.

bc_eastpost_spire_afternoon_delight.skip_reason: Only a sparse page (above Applebee, loose rock); no source states the approach line or descent.

set.approach: From the Kain hut or the Applebee campground, follow the north lateral moraine of the Bugaboo Glacier, then cross the snowfield up to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col. The climb follows the south arete from the col, starting with a long stretch of easy scrambling on ledges; carry an ice axe and possibly crampons for the snow below the col.
set.descent_text: Descend by the route itself, using rappels and scrambling. A rappel station sits at the Great Gendarme, and below the roped section the ridge is a scramble back down to the col.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; alpinedave confirms scramble then gendarme and descent along the ridge.

set.approach: The east face is reached by the Crescent Glacier. From the Kain hut, walk toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col but leave that route short of the col, exactly as for Crescent Spire; from the Applebee campground, hike north onto the moraine and follow the same line. The face is obvious from there. On that face, the line follows the central one of the three big corner systems that face left.

review.notes: Approach only; the route finishes on the northeast ridge but no descent is stated.

set.approach: From the Applebee campground go through the Crescent-Eastpost col, then drop low and traverse east beneath the Whipping Post. Scramble back up through boulders to the col between Brenta Spire and Cobalt Lake Spire. Cross snow and scree beneath the east buttress of Brenta Spire toward its northeast spur; the route begins from the snow in a moat at the foot of that spur.
set.descent_text: Follow the ridge past the main summit. A webbed rappel point on the south side of the summit leads down the east side and avoids loose, exposed fourth-class ground. Continue down the South Ridge to the next col, where a large boulder and cairn mark bolted rings for rappels down the east side; a short scramble and a final rappel lead into a moat, so an ice axe is useful. Then walk back to camp.

review.notes: Single page; counts and times omitted.

set.approach: The east face is a separate dome where the northeast face ends on the south, not far north of the Llama Peak col. It is plain from the Coldwater River side and from the Vicuna trail. One approach is to bushwhack up from the last switchback of the Coldwater road; the other is to descend from the ridge near Llama Peak.

review.notes: Single page; approach only.

set.approach: The route climbs the left part of the east face, right beside Purple People Eaters. Start from Highway 5 and take the Zupjok-Llama-Alpaca trail, descend from the saddle below Llama's south side and contour through trees, passing three gullies with waterfalls, to reach the base.
set.descent_text: From the top, scramble and bushwhack up through forest to the shelf above the east face. Cross the meadows diagonally to the south and rejoin the trail on the far side of the Llama summit.

review.notes: Single page; times omitted.

bc_alpaca_peak_al_pika_slabs.skip_reason: Page gives the start only relative to a col and no way to reach it; no descent.

set.approach: Access is from Spences Bridge: use the dirt road running alongside the railway, go beneath Highway 1 and past the waterfall, and turn uphill onto Murray Creek forest road. Park at the top of the switchbacks, cross the sagebrush benches to the talus at the foot of the southeast-facing wall, then pick your way up scree and talus to the wall itself. The route is on the central buttress.

review.notes: Area page; approach only.

set.approach: From the end of the forest road, follow the road on foot across the creek to its end, then look for pink flagging at the entrance to an open clear-cut and follow a small stream up through the marshy cut block to treeline. A faint trail leads through forest and steep sections past several wetlands to a small tarn. Go around the far end of the tarn and up a short boulder field, follow a wall to a creek and ascend its drainage to another boulder field, then bear left to enter the open alpine talus. The cliff comes into view; climb loose steep talus or snow to the base of the left-hand buttress.
set.descent_text: From the top, walk east (climber's left) to a flagged tree and work down a gully until a fixed rope takes you to an obvious ledge. Scramble the ledge right and then back left, keeping right of the gully, to a flagged tree with a flagged rappel anchor. Rappel, then follow a sloping ledge right and back left to the final rappel station, which lands on the low ridge.

review.notes: Single page; distances and rope lengths omitted.

set.approach: From the Grouse Mountain side, hike to Crown Pass and bear right down into Hanes Valley. Keep descending the talus until it is possible to traverse left onto a second slope, and climb that to the foot of the routes. The start is a large slab right of a small gully, reached by dropping about halfway toward the valley floor and climbing back up scree and talus.
set.descent_text: The route ends on top of The Camel. Rappel from there, after which a fixed-rope trail climbs to the summit of Crown Mountain. The Camel rappels go to the neck and then to the base on an overhanging line, and old slings on the blocks should be backed up with fresh webbing.

review.notes: MP page and area page plus a trip account agree on approach and Camel rappels; counts omitted.

set.approach: The most used approach is the Dewar Creek Hot Springs trail. Above the hot springs, climb the rugged hillside cross-country to the pass above, then either drop to Fry Creek and bushwhack up the steep brushy creek, or contour across the slope under Mount Twomey's walls, to reach the cirque below the east side of Hall Peak. Both ways involve heavy brush and steep talus. The route is on the east face of Hall Peak, above that cirque.

review.notes: Approach only.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route back down to the col between Hall Peak and Block Tower, with the top rappel overhanging.

review.notes: Single page for descent; rappel count omitted.
